q: remove red wine stain from wool
how to remove red wine stain from rug
best way to remove red wine stain
a: To remove a red wine stain from a white wool rug: 1. Act quickly - blot (do not rub) the stain with a clean white cloth to absorb as much wine as possible. 2. Apply salt or baking soda to the stain to absorb remaining wine. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes, then vacuum. 3. Mix a solution of 1 part white vinegar to 2 parts water. Apply to the stain with a spray bottle or cloth. Blot gently. 4. Apply a small amount of mild wool-safe detergent mixed with cold water. Blot. 5. Rinse with cold water by blotting with a damp cloth. 6. For stubborn stains, try a specialized wool stain remover like Folex or Woolite. IMPORTANT: Do NOT use boiling water on wool - it will shrink and damage the fibers. Do not rub vigorously as this can felt the wool. Do not use bleach or hydrogen peroxide on wool. Wool is naturally stain-resistant due to its lanolin coating, so gentle blotting and mild cleaners usually work. For set-in stains, professional dry cleaning may be necessary.
